by_judge.judge: D K SINGH & RAJESH RAI K
S SUNIL DUTT YADAV & PRADEEP SINGH YERUR

narrative:
On September 18, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 42.0%, resolving 1,182 cases out of the 2,812 scheduled. This represents a marginal recovery from the previous day's hearing rate of 41.5% (1,289 heard out of 3,104 scheduled) and a steady climb from the 35.8% rate observed on September 15, though it remains below the 50.8% peak achieved on September 11.

Individual judicial performance featured notable volume and strong clearance rates. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty in Hall 21 heard 62 of 87 scheduled cases (71.3%), while Justice E.S. Indiresh in Hall 18 disposed of 49 out of 63 matters (77.8%). Justice C.M. Poonacha in Hall 31 managed exceptionally large dockets across multiple lists, successfully hearing 58 out of 89 cases (65.2%) and 54 out of 106 cases (50.9%). Conversely, Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad faced heavily congested lists in Hall 7, including a major docket of 279 cases of which only 1 was heard, though he cleared 27 out of 35 (77.1%) in his more moderately sized list.

In terms of procedural stages, preliminary hearings yielded the highest conversion rate at 58.9% (168 of 285 cases), followed by admissions at 51.3% (358 of 698) and orders at 47.8% (374 of 783). Final hearings converted at 28.0% (118 of 422), showing a modest improvement from yesterday’s 23.6%. Under case-type distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the docket with 1,230 scheduled and 395 heard (32.1%), followed by Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) with a 52.6% hearing rate (240 of 456) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) at 51.1% (214 of 419).
